nodes.label: HTML element
nodes.rationale: Standard HTML5 doctype <!DOCTYPE html> prevents quirky rendering modes; <html lang> set on the primary document language and on elements using a differing language (screen reader pronunciation, translation tools, locale-sensitive features like CSS hyphens); single <h1> per page/view; <search> encloses search/filtering; DO use <button> for JS/Modals/Forms; decorative SVG images aria-hidden='true'; informative SVGs get proper accessible names.

nodes.label: lang attribute
nodes.rationale: Set on the <html> element for the primary document language and on any element that uses a language that differs from the primary language, for screen reader pronunciation and translation tools and locale-sensitive features.

nodes.label: viewport meta
nodes.rationale: The meta name=viewport element with content='width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0' for page responsiveness.

nodes.label: heading hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Sequential, non-skipping heading hierarchy (<h2> to <h3>); single <h1> per page/view (modals may have their own); documented exceptions.

nodes.label: semantic landmarks
nodes.rationale: Semantic landmarks (<header>, <nav>, <main>, <aside>, <footer>) create regional navigation for assistive technologies; <search> for search; only one banner/main/contentinfo landmark per page.

nodes.label: button element
nodes.rationale: Use <button> for triggered actions (JS, Modals, Forms) with type='button' for non-submit buttons in forms; accessible names and roles matching the interaction.

nodes.label: anchor element
nodes.rationale: <a> strictly for URL navigation; controls that redirect people have role='link'.

nodes.label: list elements
nodes.rationale: Use <ul>, <ol>, and <dl> elements for list content.

nodes.label: accessible names
nodes.rationale: All interactive elements have accessible names; roles match the interaction they facilitate (implicit or via role); controls on the same page have role='button', redirects have role='link'.

nodes.label: decorative SVGs
nodes.rationale: Hide purely decorative SVG images from assistive technology using aria-hidden='true'; decorative gets an empty alt=''. Informative SVGs (logos, data visualizations, icon buttons) get proper accessible names; complex visuals get text alternatives.

nodes.label: informative SVGs
nodes.rationale: Logos, data visualizations, and icon buttons need proper accessible names; complex visuals need an accompanying text alternative providing the same information as the visual.

nodes.label: blockquote element
nodes.rationale: Use <blockquote> for extended quotations; the cite attribute provides a machine-readable URL; <cite> in captions/attributions identifies the title of the work, not the author.

nodes.label: figure element
nodes.rationale: Self-contained content referenced from the main flow (images, code snippets, quotes) that could move to an appendix or sidebar; <figcaption> as first or last child; don't use figure for every image.

nodes.label: figcaption element
nodes.rationale: Human-readable caption or attribution for <figure>; use <cite> inside for the work title.

nodes.label: code element
nodes.rationale: Short fragments of computer code (variable names, file paths, inline snippets); wrap <code> in <pre> when displaying blocks of code.

nodes.label: pre element
nodes.rationale: Blocks of code displayed with preserved whitespace; add tabindex='0' and role='region' + accessible name when scrollable.

nodes.label: fetchpriority attribute
nodes.rationale: fetchpriority='high' elevates priority of the LCP element (hero image); fetchpriority='low' demotes non-critical trackers or later carousel items — zero-sum prioritization; don't overuse 'high'.

nodes.label: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP)
nodes.rationale: The LCP element — fetchpriority='high' targets it (e.g., hero image).

nodes.label: lazy loading
nodes.rationale: Apply loading='lazy' to off-screen images/iframes; do NOT apply to above-the-fold or hero images (delays LCP).

nodes.label: aspect ratio and layout shifts (CLS)
nodes.rationale: Specify width and height on all tags to preserve aspect ratio and prevent layout shifts (CLS); use srcset for multiple sizes; with fallback for art direction and format switching.

nodes.label: picture element
nodes.rationale: Fine-grained image control: switching between image formats, sizes, and cropping across viewport sizes (art direction).

nodes.label: dialog element
nodes.rationale: Modal overlays via .showModal() (focus trap, dim backgrounds, Esc dismiss); use closedby='any' for native light-dismiss; visible close controls for voice control users; ::backdrop styles the modal background; <form method='dialog'> dismisses without JS.

nodes.label: Popover API
nodes.rationale: popover attribute for non-modal UI (menus, tooltips) without focus traps; popovertarget toggles; don't call showModal() on popover elements; <dialog popover='auto'> combines dialog semantics with light-dismiss.

nodes.label: ::backdrop pseudo-element
nodes.rationale: Style modal backgrounds with ::backdrop.

nodes.label: form method='dialog'
nodes.rationale: Dismiss dialogs without manual JS handlers; combined formmethod='dialog' yields the button's value to dialog.returnValue.

nodes.label: details element
nodes.rationale: Native disclosure without JS; place summary as first child; details[open] for expanded styles; details::details-content for contents styling.

nodes.label: summary element
nodes.rationale: The disclosure trigger; DON'T nest interactive elements inside summary text.

nodes.label: exclusive accordions (details name)
nodes.rationale: Exclusive accordions via the name attribute on <details> inside a section with an accessible name.

nodes.label: inert attribute
nodes.rationale: Use on entire hidden sections (off-screen menus, background while a custom modal is open) to remove them from tab flow and a11y trees; pair with CSS opacity/user-select.

nodes.label: tabindex rules
nodes.rationale: No positive tabindex values (use 0 or -1 for JS programmatic focus); don't alter focus flow using CSS order/flex-flow: row-reverse.

nodes.label: form attribute
nodes.rationale: Decouple inputs from the physical <form> tree via form='form-id'.

nodes.label: datalist element
nodes.rationale: Lightweight auto-suggestions via <datalist> coupled with <input list='id'> (visually unstylable, screen-reader quirks).

nodes.label: autocomplete attribute
nodes.rationale: Use autocomplete tokens with appropriate values for personal info (autocomplete='current-password' vs 'new-password' so password managers offer the right action); don't use autocomplete='off' on credential/address/payment/contact fields.

nodes.label: inputmode attribute
nodes.rationale: Match inputmode with type and autocomplete (type='email' + inputmode='email' + autocomplete='email'); controls keyboard, validation, and autofill respectively.

nodes.label: video element
nodes.rationale: Set width/height to prevent CLS; provide a poster fallback; include subtitles/captions via <track>; background videos muted with role='none'/aria-hidden, no controls so not focusable.

nodes.label: video poster
nodes.rationale: Poster image fallback for videos.

nodes.label: video track (captions)
nodes.rationale: Subtitles and captions via <track> (kind='captions', srclang, label).

nodes.label: style attribute
nodes.rationale: Pass state to CSS via custom properties; JS provides the raw data; DON'T use inline styles for static design; DON'T convey state/information via color alone; ensure screen-reader alternatives for dynamic state.

nodes.label: addEventListener()
nodes.rationale: Trigger actions using addEventListener(); no inline event handlers (onclick).

nodes.label: aria-hidden attribute
nodes.rationale: Hide purely decorative SVG images from AT via aria-hidden='true'; decorative gets empty alt=''. Informative SVGs get proper accessible names/text alternatives.

nodes.label: role attribute
nodes.rationale: Ensure interactive elements have roles matching the interaction (implicit or via role); DON'T change native semantics with ARIA unless critical.

nodes.label: Declarative Shadow DOM (DSD)
nodes.rationale: Pre-render a custom element's markup — including its shadow tree — from the server so the component is styled and structured before any JS runs; the parser attaches the shadow root from HTML alone via <template shadowrootmode>; the element is later hydrated by its class when registered.

nodes.label: attachShadow()
nodes.rationale: Constructor must reuse the server-rendered shadow root (if (!this.shadowRoot) this.attachShadow(...)); attach behavior to the existing markup; do NOT re-render — that discards the server's DOM and flashes.

nodes.label: flash of unstyled content (FOUC)
nodes.rationale: DSD renders correctly on first paint only if styles ship inside the declarative template; use my-card:not(:defined) only for styles that must wait for JS.

nodes.label: getHTML({ serializableShadowRoots: true })
nodes.rationale: Serialize an existing shadow root back to HTML on the server/tests via getHTML({ serializableShadowRoots: true }); attach with serializable: true.

nodes.label: ShadowRootMode feature detection
nodes.rationale: In engines that don't parse shadowrootmode: Object.hasOwn(HTMLTemplateElement.prototype, 'shadowRootMode'); if absent, attach the shadow root imperatively from the same markup during upgrade so the component still renders.

nodes.label: shadow root
nodes.rationale: Encapsulated DOM subtree attached to a host: styles inside it do not leak out, and page styles do not leak in (except inherited properties).

nodes.label: delegatesFocus option
nodes.rationale: Set on attachShadow({delegatesFocus: true}) whenever the component wraps focusable controls; focusing the host moves focus to the first focusable element inside, routes :focus styling to the host, and forwards <label> clicks to the inner control on form-associated custom elements.

nodes.label: template element
nodes.rationale: Define <template> once (module scope or a static field); clone it per instance (deep-clone: cloning a parsed fragment is far faster than re-parsing innerHTML on every construction).

nodes.label: slots
nodes.rationale: Light DOM content is projected into slots; whitespace counts toward the default slot; DOM order is preserved, not slot order; slotchange is the reliable upgrade-timing signal.

nodes.label: adoptedStyleSheets
nodes.rationale: One shared CSSStyleSheet across all instances (constructed sheet; fastest at scale; no @import support); a per-instance <style> or external <link> per instance is slower.

nodes.label: :host pseudo-class
nodes.rationale: The component's own host element styled from inside its shadow tree; host-specific rules (e.g., :host([disabled])) override properties set on :host.

nodes.label: :host-context()
nodes.rationale: Chromium-only dead end (Firefox and Safari have declined to ship it); treat as not forward-looking; theme through an inherited CSS custom property instead.

nodes.label: CSS custom properties
nodes.rationale: Inherited across the shadow boundary (color, font-family, line-height, custom properties); expose them with sensible fallbacks: :host { background: var(--card-bg, white); }.

nodes.label: ::slotted()
nodes.rationale: Targets the top-level nodes assigned to a slot; cannot reach their descendants; loses to any light DOM rule — use it for light touch-ups, not control.

nodes.label: part attribute
nodes.rationale: Mark internal elements with part='name' so consumers style them via my-card::part(submit); expose a few high-level parts (not every div); forward nested parts with exportparts.

nodes.label: :state() styling
nodes.rationale: Expose internal boolean states via ElementInternals states (see custom-elements); style with :host(:state(busy)) or tag-name:state(name); read-only to consumers; prefer over data-* attributes when the component owns the state.

nodes.label: @layer
nodes.rationale: Cascade layers work inside a shadow root and are scoped to it; use to order own component styles (@layer base, theme) so consumer overrides via custom properties and ::part win predictably.

nodes.label: container queries
nodes.rationale: The right tool for responsive components: respond to the space given, not the viewport; declare the host as a container (display:block — custom elements default to inline and size containment doesn't apply to inline/contents) and query it with @container.

nodes.label: forwarding styles to wrapped native elements
nodes.rationale: Form controls don't inherit typography (color and custom properties cross the boundary, but <button>/<input>/<select> take font/color from the UA stylesheet) — set font: inherit and color: inherit on the wrapped control; :host styles don't reach the inner element; display: contents + all: inherit is the only generic pass-through, with caveats (getBoundingClientRect returns 0 for display:contents elements, breaking anchor positioning).

nodes.label: all: inherit
nodes.rationale: Resets UA defaults; scope to specific properties or use revert when defaults are wanted back.

nodes.label: display: contents
nodes.rationale: Collapsing the host is usually the point of composition (compensating for the missing built-in inheritance); broad part surfaces become brittle APIs.

nodes.label: custom elements
nodes.rationale: Encapsulated behavior, lifecycle, or a reusable JS-backed API on a tag; platform primitives (Custom Elements, Shadow DOM, HTML Templates) for reusable, framework-agnostic components whose markup and styles are encapsulated from the document. Not built when: a plain HTML element with CSS would do; purely presentational with no behavior; or only style scoping on the server with no interactivity. A like/favorite toggle qualifies: latched domain state, exposed as a styling hook, dispatches its own change event.

nodes.label: kebab-case tag names
nodes.rationale: MANDATORY: the tag name must be kebab-case with at least one hyphen — what distinguishes custom elements from current and future built-ins.

nodes.label: super() first
nodes.rationale: MANDATORY: call super() first in the constructor, before touching this (reading/writing this after super() is where it starts; throws).

nodes.label: semantic elements in shadow templates
nodes.rationale: MANDATORY: use semantic elements (button, nav, ul) inside shadow templates; a slot does not change the role of what it projects.

nodes.label: ARIA id references
nodes.rationale: MANDATORY: aria-labelledby/describedby/controls cannot cross a shadow boundary; the referencing element and the id it points to must live in the same tree.

nodes.label: mode: 'open'
nodes.rationale: MANDATORY: attachShadow({mode: 'open'}); closed hides element.shadowRoot from page scripts, test harnesses, and a11y checkers that walk shadow trees.

nodes.label: encapsulated state
nodes.rationale: The test: whether you need encapsulated state, a scriptable API, or behavior the native element can't express — not merely a different look (a styled <button> or <details> is more accessible and cheaper).

nodes.label: native elements
nodes.rationale: A plain HTML element with CSS would do; a styled <button> or <details> is more accessible and cheaper; taking a native element as far as it goes (CSS, listeners, occasional pseudo-element) is usually preferable to a custom element.

nodes.label: framework component model
nodes.rationale: When the project already has a component model (React, Vue, Svelte, ...), default to that framework's component for in-app UI; reach for custom elements only when the thing must escape or outlive the framework.

nodes.label: customized built-in elements
nodes.rationale: Avoid: extends HTMLButtonElement with is=...; Safari has permanently declined to ship them.

nodes.label: design systems
nodes.rationale: Shared primitives across apps or frameworks; embeddable widgets; output that must work as plain HTML (email, CMS, SSR fragments); don't stand up a parallel component system for ordinary in-app views.

nodes.label: static formAssociated
nodes.rationale: Set on form-associated custom elements; forwards <label> clicks to the inner control (see form-associated-custom-elements).

nodes.label: Calculating Event Differentials and Formatting Durations with Temporal
Temporal.ZonedDateTime
nodes.rationale: Zoned date-time point on the timeline in a specific zone; DST-safe differentials; .since()/.until() return Temporal.Duration.

nodes.label: Temporal.Duration
nodes.rationale: Balanced/compared durations; .round({largestUnit}) rebalances across calendar months, years, or DST with relativeTo; Temporal.Duration.compare for comparisons.

nodes.label: Intl.DurationFormat
nodes.rationale: Localized human-readable duration text via duration.toLocaleString(locale, options); use duration.toString() only for machine-readable ISO 8601 strings.

nodes.label: Temporal.Now.zonedDateTimeISO(TimeZone)
nodes.rationale: Now in the system zone or an explicit IANA zone when the target event's zone differs from the system default.

nodes.label: ZonedDateTime.since()
nodes.rationale: Elapsed time since a past event: now.since(start, {largestUnit, smallestUnit}); ZonedDateTime diffs default to largestUnit: 'hour' (days are not fixed across DST).

nodes.label: ZonedDateTime.until()
nodes.rationale: Time remaining until a future event: now.until(end, {largestUnit, smallestUnit}); smallestUnit rounds away seconds/sub-second noise.

nodes.label: Duration.round()
nodes.rationale: Rebalance/round standalone durations (Temporal.Duration.from({minutes: 90}).round({largestUnit: 'hour'})); supply relativeTo when balancing across calendar months, years, or DST transitions.

nodes.label: Duration.sign
nodes.rationale: Check sign < 0 to see a past/expired time point; the native .sign property of the computed Temporal.Duration.

nodes.label: Temporal.Duration.compare()
nodes.rationale: Compare durations; pass { relativeTo } whenever either duration has calendar units (months, years) or crosses DST boundaries.

nodes.label: Duration.toString()
nodes.rationale: Machine-readable ISO 8601 duration strings (PT1H30M); never for user-facing copy.

nodes.label: Temporal immutability
nodes.rationale: Temporal objects are immutable; .add()/.subtract()/.round()/.with() return a new instance rather than mutating.

nodes.label: Capturing Location-Agnostic Data and Partial Dates with Temporal
Temporal.PlainDate
nodes.rationale: Full calendar dates (year, month, day); birthdates, event dates, subscription billing dates.

nodes.label: Temporal.PlainTime
nodes.rationale: Wall-clock times (hour, minute, second, ...); daily alarms (9:00 AM wherever the user is), store hours.

nodes.label: Temporal.PlainDateTime
nodes.rationale: Calendar date + wall-clock time without a zone; floating local schedules; combine a PlainDate and PlainTime before attaching a zone.

nodes.label: Temporal.PlainMonthDay
nodes.rationale: Month and day without a year; recurring annual birthdays, anniversaries, fixed holidays; convert to a PlainDate with .toPlainDate({ year }) before arithmetic because month lengths vary by year.

nodes.label: Temporal.PlainYearMonth
nodes.rationale: Year and month without a day; credit card expirations (2027-12), monthly billing periods; compare with Temporal.PlainYearMonth.compare.

nodes.label: Temporal.Instant
nodes.rationale: Exact point on the UTC timeline with nanosecond precision; unambiguous (see sort-high-precision-timestamps for parsing, sorting, and intervals).

nodes.label: Temporal.Now.plainDateISO()
nodes.rationale: Current date for location-agnostic comparison; convert to PlainMonthDay/PlainYearMonth with .toPlainMonthDay()/toPlainYearMonth().

nodes.label: overflow: 'constrain'
nodes.rationale: PlainDate.add() default: clamps month-end dates like Jan 31 to Feb 28/29.

nodes.label: overflow: 'reject'
nodes.rationale: Throw a RangeError when the target day does not exist (e.g., day 31 in February).

nodes.label: PlainDate.toPlainDateTime()
nodes.rationale: Combine a calendar date and wall-clock without interpolating ISO strings (e.g., Temporal.PlainDate.from(dateStr).toPlainDateTime(timeStr).toZonedDateTime(tz)).

nodes.label: PlainMonthDay.toPlainDate()
nodes.rationale: Convert an annual recurrence to a PlainDate with a specific year before doing arithmetic (month lengths depend on leap years).

nodes.label: calendar parameter (e.g., 'iso8601')
nodes.rationale: Specify explicitly when constructing PlainMonthDay or non-ISO Plain types from object bags, and when working with non-ISO calendars; ISO 8601 is the default when parsing ISO strings or constructing from property bags.

nodes.label: location-agnostic Plain types
nodes.rationale: The core concept: Plain types carry no time zone offset and represent calendar dates/wall-clock times exactly as read off a calendar or clock; data stays identical regardless of the viewer's location; pick the narrowest type (PlainDate > PlainTime > PlainDateTime > PlainMonthDay > PlainYearMonth).

nodes.label: Temporal.ZonedDateTime
nodes.rationale: DST-safe calendar-aware scheduling; for events bound to a specific geographical location (e.g., a meeting in a specific city).

nodes.label: disambiguation option
nodes.rationale: Controls behavior when a time is ambiguous or does not exist (e.g., during clock changes): 'reject' throws RangeError to detect conflicts; 'compatible' (default) resolves to a valid time.

nodes.label: ZonedDateTime.withTimeZone()
nodes.rationale: Convert to the equivalent time in another location (e.g., Asia/Tokyo); non-mutating — returns a new instance.

nodes.label: Temporal.Now.zonedDateTimeISO(TimeZone)
nodes.rationale: Now in the system zone or an explicit zone when the target event's zone differs.

nodes.label: ZonedDateTime.toLocaleString()
nodes.rationale: User-facing display (e.g., { hour: 'numeric', minute: '2-digit' }) instead of manual hour/minute padding.

nodes.label: PlainDateTime not for global events
nodes.rationale: DO NOT use PlainDateTime for global events — it doesn't carry zone info and can't account for DST changes.

nodes.label: structuredClone()
nodes.rationale: Use structuredClone(value) to deep-copy nested objects, arrays, and built-in platform types (Date, Map, Set, TypedArrays, BigInt, cyclic references, shared DAG refs) without a JSON round-trip; throws DataCloneError on functions/symbols/DOM nodes.

nodes.label: JSON.parse(JSON.stringify()) workaround
nodes.rationale: Legacy userland workaround replaced by structuredClone() when callers don't depend on JSON wire normalization (toJSON, replacers, revivers).

nodes.label: array.toSorted()
nodes.rationale: Use instead of [...array].sort() — returns a new array without mutating the source.

nodes.label: array.toReversed()
nodes.rationale: Use instead of [...array].reverse() — non-mutating reverse.

nodes.label: array.toSpliced()
nodes.rationale: Immutable insertions/deletions/replacements instead of clone+splice.

nodes.label: array.with()
nodes.rationale: Single-index immutable updates instead of copy+assign.

nodes.label: array.findLast()
nodes.rationale: Use instead of [...array].reverse().find(); passes the original forward index to the callback.

nodes.label: array.findLastIndex()
nodes.rationale: Use instead of reversing and searching; returns -1 on miss (vs out-of-bounds on reversed-copy searches).

nodes.label: Array.from()/[...] conversion
nodes.rationale: Convert strings, Sets, NodeLists, generators, arguments, array-likes to real arrays first: .toSorted() on non-arrays throws TypeError. Also note typed-array sort is numeric (not string coercion), and TypedArrays lack toSpliced/toReversed sparse-hole caveats.

nodes.label: Object.groupBy()
nodes.rationale: Use Object.groupBy(items, (item, index) => key) instead of reduce bucket accumulators; returns a null-prototype object; CreateDataProperty so 'constructor'/'toString' keys never collide; use Object.hasOwn or ?? [] when reading buckets.

nodes.label: Map.groupBy()
nodes.rationale: Use Map.groupBy when grouping by object references or non-string keys whose String() coercion must be avoided; preserves number/boolean/BigInt/undefined keys.

nodes.label: Promise.withResolvers()
nodes.rationale: Use when resolve/reject must be stored or invoked outside the new Promise executor scope (event listeners, stream queues, cancellation tokens).

nodes.label: AbortSignal.timeout()
nodes.rationale: Time-bounded async operations; aborts with TimeoutError (not AbortError). DO NOT pass negative/0-arg values.

nodes.label: AbortSignal.any()
nodes.rationale: Combine user cancellation with a deadline; the composite signal aborts when the first input signal aborts and propagates its reason.

nodes.label: Error cause options ({ cause })
nodes.rationale: Pass { cause: err } to new Error(message, { cause: err }) when wrapping and re-throwing across layers; check both 'TimeoutError' and 'AbortError' when distinguishing deadline from user cancellation.

nodes.label: URLSearchParams
nodes.rationale: Parse/construct/mutate query strings (new URL(fullUrl, base).searchParams); preserves '=' in values and '+' semantics; use Object.fromEntries(params) — last value wins on duplicate keys.

nodes.label: TextDecoder
nodes.rationale: Decode UTF-8 byte buffers to text; use { fatal: true } to throw TypeError on invalid sequences; reuse with { stream: true } for chunked streams.

nodes.label: TextEncoder
nodes.rationale: Encode strings to UTF-8 Uint8Array byte arrays instead of manual character-code loops.

nodes.label: streaming TextDecoder
nodes.rationale: For chunked streams (ReadableStream, WebSocket frames, file chunks): stream: true during chunks, final decode() flush after.

nodes.label: element.replaceChildren()
nodes.rationale: Atomic child replacement/clearing; batches mutations into a single MutationObserver record; template.content.replaceChildren() for templates.

nodes.label: innerHTML='' clearing workaround
nodes.rationale: Legacy workarounds (innerHTML = '' clearing loops) are eliminated by replaceChildren().

nodes.label: new Event()/new CustomEvent()
nodes.rationale: Use constructors for events instead of document.createEvent()/initEvent()/initCustomEvent(); use CustomEvent detail for payloads; set composed: true when crossing a shadow DOM boundary.

nodes.label: Temporal.Instant
nodes.rationale: Exact point on the UTC timeline with nanosecond precision; browsers clamp Temporal.Now.instant() to ms/µs (Spectre timing-attack mitigation); use Temporal.Instant.from() for server/native clocks.

nodes.label: Temporal.Instant.from()
nodes.rationale: Parse recorded ISO strings with the full nanosecond value; keep the source-recorded timestamp; don't replace with Temporal.Now.instant() in the browser.

nodes.label: Temporal.Instant.compare()
nodes.rationale: Comparator comparing the full nanosecond value; use for Array.sort()/toSorted(); returns -1, 0, or 1.

nodes.label: Instant.equals()
nodes.rationale: Detect identical timestamps; don't check compare() === 0 or compare .toString() output.

nodes.label: Instant.since()
nodes.rationale: Temporal.Duration between consecutive events; retains nanosecond precision.

nodes.label: Temporal.Duration
nodes.rationale: Exact nanosecond-precision interval between instants (from since()); display with duration.toLocaleString(); don't collapse to a single Number (total('nanoseconds') exceeds Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER for spans > ~104 days).

nodes.label: performance.now()
nodes.rationale: Measure sub-millisecond intervals in the client; browsers clamp Temporal.Now.instant() to ms/µs; also use performance.mark().

nodes.label: Instant.toZonedDateTimeISO(TimeZone)
nodes.rationale: Display the localized wall-clock time of an event to a user when needed.

nodes.label: Supporting Global Calendar Systems with Temporal
withCalendar()
nodes.rationale: Associate a calendar system with a Temporal object (mandatory) for calendar-sensitive operations.

nodes.label: Temporal.PlainDate
nodes.rationale: Full calendar dates on the ISO 8601 calendar; the type SGC_MD's other concepts operate on (e.g., withCalendar on instances of it).

nodes.label: monthCode
nodes.rationale: Stable month identifier across leap years for lunisolar calendars (Hebrew/Chinese leap months); use for identifying specific months regardless of year; don't assume date.month === 12 is the last month.

nodes.label: monthsInYear
nodes.rationale: Upper bound when iterating months (don't assume 12); date.month === monthsInYear identifies the last month.

nodes.label: daysInMonth
nodes.rationale: Days per month; don't assume fixed values (e.g., 31) or assume inLeapYear implies +1 day (lunisolar leap years add a full leap month).

nodes.label: inLeapYear
nodes.rationale: True when the calendar year is a leap year; in lunisolar calendars it may add a full leap month.

nodes.label: Temporal.PlainDate.compare()
nodes.rationale: Calendar-aware comparisons; use instead of comparing year/month/day properties manually; correctly handles chronological ordering within the calendar rules.

nodes.label: Intl.supportedValuesOf('calendar')
nodes.rationale: Verify the target calendar system is supported by the environment before creating calendar-specific Temporal objects.

nodes.label: supported calendar systems
nodes.rationale: Islamic (lunar), Hebrew (lunisolar), Chinese (lunisolar); some (variants of the Islamic calendar) rely on visual observation rather than fixed calculations — Temporal follows the environment's Intl implementation (usually calculated approximations); verify with domain experts or specialized libraries for cultural/religious date calculations; account for era names (Japanese, Buddhist) via toLocaleString.

nodes.label: with({ month: m })
nodes.rationale: Safe month iteration: targetDate.with({ month: m }).daysInMonth.

nodes.label: toLocaleString() with era
nodes.rationale: Include the era for era-based calendars like 'japanese' (Japanese, Buddhist eras).

nodes.label: Debounce and batch multiple analytics events
fetchLater()
nodes.rationale: Debounce and batch analytics events: schedule with activateAfter; a new event aborts the pending beacon and re-schedules; the browser reliably sends the latest payload if the user leaves/closes; wrap in try/catch for quota errors; check fetchLaterResult.activated when resetting queues.

nodes.label: activateAfter option
nodes.rationale: Schedules the fetchLater() beacon after this delay (e.g., 10s); abort previous pending beacons; use when a new analytics event occurs.

nodes.label: fetchLater() result
nodes.rationale: Returned object; .activated is true after the beacon is sent; used to reset the event queue.

nodes.label: AbortController
nodes.rationale: Cancel the pending beacon in cases where a new analytics event occurs.

nodes.label: MAX_QUEUE_SIZE
nodes.rationale: Cap on queued events (e.g., 100) — pick a number unlikely to overflow the fetchLater() quota.

nodes.label: fetchLater() quota
nodes.rationale: Currently roughly 64KB per origin; wrap fetchLater() calls in try/catch to handle quota errors.

nodes.label: navigator.sendBeacon()
nodes.rationale: Polyfill fallback: sends the payload when visibilityState changes to 'hidden' (the most reliable end-of-session signal); uses fetch keepalive if the browser supports it.

nodes.label: scheduler.yield()
nodes.rationale: Pauses a running task so the browser can handle pending user input and rendering before continuing; use in async functions with a 50ms deadline reset.

nodes.label: scheduler.postTask()
nodes.rationale: Schedule work at different priorities; continuations automatically inherit the enclosing task's priority and TaskSignal.

nodes.label: TaskController
nodes.rationale: Abort and reprioritize queued tasks.

nodes.label: TaskSignal
nodes.rationale: Continuations inherit the enclosing task's priority and TaskSignal; used with scheduler.yield() inside long postTask tasks.

nodes.label: setTimeout yield fallback
nodes.rationale: Fallback: feature-detect scheduler.yield; use await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 0)) when unsupported.

nodes.label: 50ms long-task budget
nodes.rationale: Deadline = performance.now() + 50 (the boundary for when a task becomes a long task); when exceeded, await scheduler.yield() and reset the deadline.

nodes.label: VisibilityStateEntry
nodes.rationale: Performance timeline entry recording visibility changes (entry.name === 'visible'/'hidden', entry.startTime); accessed via performance.getEntriesByType('visibility-state').

nodes.label: visibility-state performance timeline entries
nodes.rationale: Query the entire visibility history at any time with performance.getEntriesByType('visibility-state').

nodes.label: total foreground time
nodes.rationale: Sum of durations where name === 'visible'; the final visible period ends at performance.now(); fallback returns performance.now() when the entries array is empty (API unsupported).

nodes.label: performance.now()
nodes.rationale: Used for the final visible period's end; fallback when VisibilityStateEntry is unsupported: total time since navigation start (a reasonable upper bound).

nodes.label: top-level await
nodes.rationale: Pauses module execution to await promises; encapsulates conditional loading of polyfills or heavy secondary libraries only when required by the browser.

nodes.label: dynamic import()
nodes.rationale: Conditional dependency loading (e.g., await import('/path/to/popover-polyfill.js')); awaited at the top level of a dedicated module so consumers wait until the dependency is ready.

nodes.label: feature detection (HTMLElement.prototype)
nodes.rationale: MANDATORY: prefer checking HTMLElement.prototype over window or document when checking a global DOM attribute/property like popover.

nodes.label: single entry module pattern
nodes.rationale: When the entry module runs dependent initialization directly: statically import the top-level-await module at the top of the entry and run code in its body; DO NOT use sibling static imports (they evaluate concurrently with the entry).

nodes.label: chained dynamic imports with top-level await
nodes.rationale: When the entry delegates to app modules: await import('./conditionally-load-polyfill.js'); await import('./app.js').

nodes.label: conditional polyfill pattern
nodes.rationale: The central pattern: check feature presence, then await import of the polyfill — encapsulates detection in the dependency module.

nodes.label: legacy async orchestration fallback
nodes.rationale: Legacy browsers without top-level await support: avoid TLA; wrap conditional import() orchestration in an async function or .then() promise chain.

nodes.label: content-visibility: auto
nodes.rationale: Browser automatically offloads layout/paint workload until the container scrolls close to view; pair with contain-intrinsic-size; DO NOT apply to elements within the initial fold (paradoxically delays critical page load).

nodes.label: contain-intrinsic-size
nodes.rationale: Placeholder dimension (e.g., auto none auto 150px); the 'auto' keyword makes the browser remember the actual size after render, avoiding layout shifts.

nodes.label: content-visibility: hidden
nodes.rationale: Skips layout calculations for hidden divs while preserving style containment; supercedes display:none for toggling; excludes content from the accessibility tree and find-in-page — DO NOT use if content must remain discoverable while hidden.

nodes.label: hidden='until-found' attribute
nodes.rationale: Searchable & deferred rendering (collapsible disclosures); see search-hidden-content for find-in-page accessibility.

nodes.label: defer-rendering strategy
nodes.rationale: Below the fold (content-visibility: auto) vs toggle state (content-visibility: hidden) vs searchable & deferred (hidden='until-found').

nodes.label: scroll event
nodes.rationale: Use only for basic dynamic metrics or informative layout styling; do NOT execute heavy work here.

nodes.label: scrollend event
nodes.rationale: Reliable signal when a scroll has rested, transitions finished, and a touch gesture released; execute expensive work (fetches, layout recalcs) here.

nodes.label: scrollSnapChange
nodes.rationale: Consider pairing with snap interactions (carousels, testimonial galleries) — scrollSnapChanging for the in-progress signal.

nodes.label: scrollSnapChanging
nodes.rationale: scrollSnapChanging companion for snap interactions.

nodes.label: image-set()
nodes.rationale: Browser picks the smallest compatible image at the appropriate pixel density; provide modern formats (AVIF, WebP) alongside resolutions (1x, 2x); always order formats from most optimized (AVIF) to least optimized; CAUTION: images in CSS are not discoverable by the preload scanner — LCP candidates should use HTML / or preload with a media attribute.

nodes.label: optimized decorative images
nodes.rationale: Doc thesis: delivering optimized decorative images via CSS improves perceived performance without sacrificing visual quality.

nodes.label: background-image
nodes.rationale: Used with image-set() (most commonly), also content and mask-image.

nodes.label: fetch priority option
nodes.rationale: Add priority: 'low' to the fetch() init for background analytics/beacons/prefetch; DO NOT use priority: 'low' for critical UI fetches; DO NOT use the deprecated 'importance' key.

nodes.label: critical fetches
nodes.rationale: User-impacting fetches: UI updates, user-initiated actions; priority: 'low' prohibited.

nodes.label: background fetches
nodes.rationale: Analytics, logging, or background synchronization — deprioritized so critical fetches complete faster.

nodes.label: VisibilityStateEntry
nodes.rationale: Use performance.getEntriesByType('visibility-state') for the exact visibility history; don't rely solely on document.visibilityState at execution time (race conditions: a background page can be foregrounded before async scripts run, and the fallback timestamp lacks the internal precision of the Performance API).

nodes.label: initial visibility state
nodes.rationale: Determines if the page was initially loaded in the background (e.g., opened in a new background tab); identify to filter out of performance analytics. The fallback (document.visibilityState === 'hidden' at script execution) is highly inaccurate for initial background state due to the race described above.

nodes.label: visibilitychange event
nodes.rationale: Fallback listener; performance.now() gives the event-listener fire time (less precise than the browser's internal change time); used to capture timeBackgrounded if hidden and null.

nodes.label: document.visibilityState
nodes.rationale: Fallback property: reads the current state at script execution (susceptible to the race).

nodes.label: content-visibility: auto
nodes.rationale: Browser skips rendering calcs when far outside the viewport (pre-render margin); use contentvisibilityautostatechange to know when the browser starts rendering before content is on screen; pair with contain-intrinsic-size to avoid scrollbar jumping.

nodes.label: contain-intrinsic-size
nodes.rationale: Placeholder size (e.g., 500px); the 'auto' keyword makes the browser remember the actual size once rendered.

nodes.label: contentvisibilityautostatechange event
nodes.rationale: Fires on the content-visibility:auto element when the browser skips (event.skipped = true) or is about to render; pause/resume heavy work (canvas animations, WebGL rendering, WebSocket polling) just-in-time.

nodes.label: IntersectionObserver
nodes.rationale: Use for application logic tied to exact visual visibility (lazy-loading data, infinite scroll triggers); use contentvisibilityautostatechange for rendering-heavy work; does not bubble — attach directly or use a capturing listener.

nodes.label: canvas/WebGL rendering
nodes.rationale: Heavy background canvas animations/WebGL rendering to pause and resume via the event.

nodes.label: WebSocket data polling
nodes.rationale: High-frequency WebSocket polling to pause when skipped and resume just-in-time when the browser prepares to display the content.

nodes.label: capturing listener fallback
nodes.rationale: contentvisibilityautostatechange may not bubble in some implementations; attach directly to the element or use { capture: true } delegation.

nodes.label: Faster SPA View Transitions via State Caching
SPA view state caching
nodes.rationale: Cache the rendered state of inactive views (content-visibility: hidden + position: absolute) instead of destroying them; CPU savings massive (browser skips layout/paint for hidden views); RAM cost high (DOM nodes, listeners, and state retained); DO for simple 3-5 view apps; DO NOT unconditionally cache in dynamic apps; MUST implement an LRU eviction strategy in highly dynamic apps.

nodes.label: content-visibility: hidden
nodes.rationale: Hides the element's contents but the element itself remains styled and visible (background, borders, padding, margins still painted); retains cached rendering state in memory for instant restores; inert + aria-hidden should accompany it.

nodes.label: aria-hidden attribute
nodes.rationale: Set on inactive views so hidden interface elements are excluded from AT.

nodes.label: inert attribute
nodes.rationale: Set on hidden views to remove interface elements from the tab order.

nodes.label: view focus management
nodes.rationale: Move focus to the new view on switch to ensure a logical tab order.

nodes.label: eviction strategy (LRU)
nodes.rationale: MANDATORY for highly dynamic apps; destroy old views when a memory threshold is reached; DO NOT unconditionally cache in dynamic apps.

nodes.label: blocking="render"
nodes.rationale: Head scripts: parsing continues but rendering waits until the resource has been fetched and executed; same render-blocking behavior as stylesheets; use on experiment scripts whose output must be visible in the initial render; DO NOT use outside <head>; pair async + type='module' (module scripts preferred for inline).

nodes.label: async + module scripts
nodes.rationale: async for external scripts (DOM built in parallel); module scripts are deferred by default and block rendering until executed.

nodes.label: anti-flicker snippet fallback
nodes.rationale: Fallback when blocking=render is unsupported: hide the page via opacity: 0 until the experiment script finishes or a 4s timeout; feature-detect HTMLScriptElement.prototype 'blocking'; reveal via onExperimentReady; DO NOT combine with blocking=render.

nodes.label: data attribute on <html>/<body>
nodes.rationale: Signal the active variant via a data attribute on <html> or <body>; CSS selectors keyed to it avoid direct DOM manipulation in the render-blocking script.

nodes.label: experiment performance monitoring
nodes.rationale: Monitor LCP/FCP to ensure the render-blocking script isn't adding excessive delay; third-party CDN outages can block rendering entirely (no dev-controlled timeout); consider server-side A/B testing to eliminate flicker.

nodes.label: Reliably measure full-session analytics and telemetry
fetchLater()
nodes.rationale: Most reliably way to send data to a server when a response isn't required and delivery timing isn't urgent (analytics, telemetry, error tracking, performance metrics like Core Web Vitals); browser sends the latest payload on navigation/tab close; wrap in try/catch for quota errors.

nodes.label: fetchLater() quota
nodes.rationale: Currently roughly 64KB per origin; minimize payload size.

nodes.label: unload-based pixel beacon technique
nodes.rationale: Older technique: creating an pixel in an unload event listener; notoriously unreliable (especially on mobile); negatively impacts performance by making pages ineligible for bfcache.

nodes.label: bfcache (Back/Forward Cache)
nodes.rationale: A page made ineligible by unload pixels can't be cached/reused; fetchLater keeps pages eligible.

nodes.label: performance.now()
nodes.rationale: Measure the session duration: sessionData.duration = performance.now() every 10s.

nodes.label: session duration
nodes.rationale: Doc example: sessionData = { duration: 0, id: crypto.randomUUID() }; setInterval(queueBeacon, 10000).

nodes.label: crypto.randomUUID()
nodes.rationale: Session/beacon ID generation in the example.

nodes.label: Long Animation Frames API
nodes.rationale: Lightweight API to identify heavy-running JavaScript in the field; emits long-animation-frame entries when a frame takes >50ms to render; used in production analytics.

nodes.label: long-animation-frame performance entries
nodes.rationale: Emitted when an animation frame takes >50ms to render; contains the duration of the frame and the scripts executed during it (entry.scripts).

nodes.label: PerformanceObserver
nodes.rationale: Monitors long-animation-frame entries (buffered: true captures entries before registration).

nodes.label: PerformanceScript objects
nodes.rationale: Each entry.scripts item: sourceURL and duration of the script executed during the long animation frame; used for grouping by script and sorting by total duration; example filters scripts with totalDuration > 100ms.

nodes.label: heavy script duration threshold
nodes.rationale: Example threshold: scripts with totalDuration > 100ms are heavy offenders; sorted by total duration so the worst offenders appear first.

nodes.label: JS Self-Profiling API
nodes.rationale: Avoided: the Long Animation Frames API is preferred because the JS Self-Profiling API carries higher runtime overhead.
